s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral erosions with systemic symptoms and a mediastinal mass
key_facts: Patient is a White man in his 50s
Oral erosions began 2 years before presentation
Weight loss of 5 kg due to impaired intake
Lingual biopsy showed epidermal acanthosis and basal-layer vacuolation
Direct immunofluorescence showed fibrinogen deposition along basement membrane
Decreased IgG serum level
Decreased total B lymphocyte count
Increased CD8+ T count with inverted CD4:CD8 ratio
Mediastinal mass was a type AB thymoma, Masaoka-Koga stage 2A

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic oral erosions and autoantibody profile

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed type AB thymoma, Masaoka-Koga stage 2A

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Skin and mucosal involvement with lymphocytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Sjogren's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic oral erosions and decreased IgG serum level

raw.rationale: The patient's oral erosions, lingual biopsy showing epidermal acanthosis and basal-layer vacuolation, and direct immunofluorescence showing fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane are consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus, which is often associated with underlying neoplasms such as the type AB thymoma found in this patient.

rejected.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
rejected.why: While pemphigus vulgaris can cause oral erosions, the presence of a mediastinal mass and the specific immunofluorescence findings point more towards paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.label: Thymoma
rejected.why: Thymoma is the underlying neoplasm but does not directly explain the oral erosions and skin findings.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Mycosis fungoides typically presents with skin lesions and does not usually cause the specific oral and immunofluorescence findings seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Sjogren's syndrome
rejected.why: Sjogren's syndrome can cause oral dryness and mucosal lesions but does not typically present with the specific biopsy and immunofluorescence findings seen in this patient.
